processed_hadiths.arabicText: قَالَ ابْنُ وَهْبٍ ، عن مَالِكٍ ، عن الْعَلَاءِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ أَبَا السَّائِبِ يُحَدِّثُ ، عن أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ : قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ : " مَنْ أَدْرَكَ مِنَ الصُّبْحِ رَكْعَةً قَبْلَ أَنْ تَطْلُعَ الشَّمْسُ ، فَقَدْ أَدْرَكَ الصُّبْحَ ، وَمَنْ أَدْرَكَ مِنَ الْعَصْرِ رَكْعَةً قَبْلَ أَنْ تَغْرُبَ الشَّمْسُ ، فَقَدْ أَدْرَكَ الْعَصْرِ "
processed_hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Abu Hurayrah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Whoever catches one rak'ah of Subh (Fajr prayer) before the sun rises, has caught Subh. And whoever catches one rak'ah of 'Asr before the sun sets, has caught 'Asr.'

processed_hadiths.arabicText: قَالَ : وَقَالَ مَالِكٌ : مَنْ جَاءَ وَالْإِمَامُ رَاكِعٌ ، فَلْيَرْكَعْ إِنْ خَشِيَ أَنْ يَرْفَعَ الْإِمَامُ رَأْسَهُ إِذَا كَانَ قَرِيبًا يَطْمَعُ إِذَا رَكَعَ ، فَدَبَّ رَاكِعًا أَنْ يَصِلَ إِلَى الصَّفِّ ، فَإِنْ كَانَ بَعِيدًا لَا يَطْمَعُ أَنْ يَصِلَ إِلَى الصَّفِّ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَرْفَعَ الْإِمَامُ رَأْسَهُ ، فَلَا يَرْكَعْ حَتَّى يَصِلَ إِلَى الصَّفِّ ، قِيلَ : وَلَا يَكُونُ مُدْرِكًا لِتِلْكَ الرَّكْعَةِ إِذَا أَدْرَكَ الْإِمَامَ رَاكِعًا ، قَالَ : لَا
processed_hadiths.english_translation: Malik said: 'Whoever comes while the imam is in ruku' (bowing), let him bow if he fears that the imam will raise his head, if he is close and hopes that by bowing and moving while bowed, he can reach the row. But if he is far and does not hope to reach the row before the imam raises his head, then let him not bow until he reaches the row.' It was asked: 'Will he not have caught that rak'ah if he caught the imam in ruku'?' He said: 'No.'

potential_issues.issue: This is a statement from Imam Malik (athar), not a prophetic narration
potential_issues.impact: This represents Malik's juristic opinion about joining congregational prayer. It is not a marfu' hadith but rather a scholarly position (madhab). No chain analysis applicable.

processed_hadiths.arabicText: قَالَ : وَقَالَ مَالِكٌ فِي الرُّكُوعِ وَالسُّجُودِ : إِذَا أَمْكَنَ يَدَيْهِ مِنْ رُكْبَتَيْهِ ، وَإِنْ لَمْ يُسَبِّحْ ، فَذَلِكَ مُجْزِئٌ عنهُ ، وَكَانَ لَا يُوَقِّتُ تَسْبِيحًا . قَالَ : وَقَالَ مَالِكٌ : التَّسْبِيحُ فِي السُّجُودِ أَيْضًا مِثْلُ الرُّكُوعِ ، وَمَنْ أَمْكَنَ جَبْهَتَهُ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ ، وَإِنْ لَمْ يُسَبِّحْ ، فَذَلِكَ مُجْزِئٌ عنهُ
processed_hadiths.english_translation: Malik said regarding ruku' and sujud: 'If one places his hands on his knees, even if he does not perform tasbih (glorification), that is sufficient for him, and he (Malik) did not specify a required number of tasbih.' And Malik said: 'Tasbih in sujud is also like ruku', and whoever places his forehead on the ground, even if he does not perform tasbih, that is sufficient for him.'

potential_issues.impact: This represents Malik's juristic opinion about the minimum requirements for valid ruku' and sujud. It is not a marfu' hadith but rather a scholarly position (madhab). No chain analysis applicable.

processed_hadiths.arabicText: قَالَ ابْنُ الْقَاسِمِ : الَّذِي أَرَى وَآخُذُ بِهِ فِي نَفْسِي فِي الَّذِي يَنْعَسُ خَلْفَ الْإِمَامِ فِي الرَّكْعَةِ الْأُولَى ، أَنَّهُ لَا يَتْبَعُ الْإِمَامَ فِيهَا , وَإِنْ كَانَ يُدْرِكُهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَرْكَعَ لِلثَّانِيَةِ ، وَإِذَا رَكَعَ لِلثَّانِيَةِ ، رَكَعَ مَعَهُ ، فَكَانَتْ لَهُ أَوَّلَ رَكْعَةٍ لَهُ ، وَهِيَ آخِرَةٌ لِلْإِمَامِ
processed_hadiths.english_translation: Ibn al-Qasim said: 'What I see and take for myself regarding the one who dozes off behind the imam in the first rak'ah is that he should not follow the imam in it, even if he catches up with him before he bows for the second (rak'ah). And when he (the imam) bows for the second (rak'ah), he (the one who dozed) should bow with him, and it will be his first rak'ah, while it is the last for the imam.'

potential_issues.issue: This is a statement from Ibn al-Qasim (a student of Malik), not a prophetic narration
potential_issues.impact: This represents Ibn al-Qasim's juristic opinion about the ruling for someone who dozes off during prayer. It is not a marfu' hadith but rather a scholarly position. No chain analysis applicable.

processed_hadiths.arabicText: قَالَ : وَقَالَ مَالِكٌ : الْجُلُوسُ فِيمَا بَيْنَ السَّجْدَتَيْنِ مثل الْجُلُوسِ فِي التَّشَهُّدِ يُفْضِي بِأَلْيَتَيْهِ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ ، وَيَنْصِبُ رِجْلَهُ الْيَمِينَ ، وَيَثْنِي رِجْلَهُ الْيُسْرَى . قَالَ : قُلْتُ : وَالتَّشَهُّدُ فِي ذَلِكَ الْجُلُوسِ ؟ قَالَ : مَا أَعْرِفُ ذَلِكَ
processed_hadiths.english_translation: Malik said: 'The sitting between the two prostrations is like the sitting in tashahhud - one lets his buttocks touch the ground, keeps his right foot upright, and folds his left foot.' I asked: 'And the tashahhud in that sitting?' He said: 'I do not know of that.'

processed_hadiths.arabicText: قُلْتُ لِابْنِ الْقَاسِمِ : فَمَا قَوْلُ مَالِكٍ فِي سُجُودِ الرَّجُلِ فِي صَلَاتِهِ ، هَلْ يَرْفَعُ بَطْنَهُ عن فَخِذَيْهِ وَيُجَافِي بِضَبْعَيْهِ ؟ قَالَ : نَعَمْ ، وَلَا يُفَرِّجُ ذَلِكَ التَّفْرِيجَ الشَّدِيدَ ، إِلَّا أَنْ يَرْفَعَ بَطْنَهُ وَيُجَافِي ضَبْعَيْهِ ، وَلَا يَتَّقِي بِيَدَيْهِ ، وَلَكِنْ يُفْضِي بِهِمَا إِلَى الْأَرْضِ ، وَالْمَرْأَةُ مِثْلُ الرَّجُلِ فِي ذَلِكَ ، إِلَّا أَنَّ الْمَرْأَةَ تَضُمُّ بَعْضَهَا إِلَى بَعْضٍ
processed_hadiths.english_translation: I asked Ibn al-Qasim: 'What is Malik's opinion about a man's prostration in his prayer - should he lift his belly from his thighs and separate his upper arms?' He said: 'Yes, but not excessive spreading, except that he lifts his belly and separates his upper arms, and he should not support himself on his hands but rather place them flat on the ground. And the woman is like the man in this, except that the woman gathers herself together.'

potential_issues.issue: This is a statement from Ibn al-Qasim reporting Malik's opinion (athar), not a prophetic narration
